title: Wolf Cola: A Public Relations Nightmare

jokes.text: Frank is discovered doing cocaine first thing in the morning, mid-dance, while the gang watches silently
jokes.setup: Someone is described as 'chipper this morning' — the gang has apparently been watching Frank without him noticing
jokes.punchline: 'Is doing cocaine every morning your routine, Frank?' — delivered deadpan, confirming this is completely normal for Frank
jokes.explanation: Perfect character-integrated cold open joke. The reveal that everyone was just quietly watching Frank do morning cocaine is a strong visual gag. Dee's deadpan question treats it as a scheduling curiosity rather than a crisis, which is pitch-perfect for the show's ethos. High character integration because this is 100% a Frank joke.

dialogue.line: Is doing cocaine every morning your routine, Frank?

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Yeah.

jokes.text: 'Is doing cocaine every morning your routine, Frank?'
jokes.setup: The gang has been watching Frank do cocaine all morning without saying anything
jokes.punchline: Dee's flat, matter-of-fact question treats cocaine as a mere scheduling quirk to confirm
jokes.explanation: The phrasing 'your routine' is doing the heavy lifting — it frames cocaine use as equivalent to making coffee. Good economy, though it slightly overlaps with joke #1.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Well, somebody's chipper this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Oh... you guys were there all this time? I didn't see you.

jokes.text: Frank says he's selling Wolf Cola to 'the Jews in Boca Raton' who are 'slurping it up like candy' and are 'addicted'
jokes.setup: Asked how Wolf Cola is doing, Frank gives a sales update
jokes.punchline: Frank's casual, enthusiastic anti-Semitic framing of a business success — delivered with zero self-awareness
jokes.explanation: Classic Frank obliviousness — his casual bigotry is the joke, not the bigotry itself. The comedy comes from the gap between Frank's cheerful business enthusiasm and the audience's dawning horror. Works because it's immediately about to bite him enormously.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: I'm selling it to the Jews in Boca Raton. They're slurping it up like candy. They're... I'm telling you, they're addicted.

jokes.text: 'Boca Raton, Frank? Or the official soft drink of Boko Haram?'
jokes.setup: Frank has been proudly describing Wolf Cola as the 'official drink of Boca Raton' — a news report reveals it's actually the official drink of Boko Haram
jokes.punchline: Dennis's perfectly constructed rhetorical contrast between the Florida retirement city and the terrorist organization
jokes.explanation: This is the best-constructed joke in the episode. The setup is built across a full minute of Frank's oblivious boasting, and Dennis delivers the callback with perfect economy — the juxtaposition of 'Boca Raton' (Jewish retirees) and 'Boko Haram' (African terrorist organization) is both horrifying and hilarious. The near-homophony of the two names is the structural genius the whole cold open rests on. Highly quotable, strong rewatch value. Earns its 8+ score.

dialogue.line: Boca Raton, Frank? Or the official soft drink of Boko Haram?

jokes.text: Frank's single-word response to discovering his soda is the official drink of a terrorist organization: 'Whoops.'
jokes.setup: Frank has just been confronted with the news that Wolf Cola is Boko Haram's official drink
jokes.punchline: 'Whoops.' — the most catastrophically insufficient response imaginable
jokes.explanation: One word. Maximum economy. The catastrophic understatement of 'Whoops' in response to being the official soda of a terrorist organization is a masterclass in character comedy — it perfectly encapsulates Frank's moral bankruptcy and utter lack of appropriate affect. The beat before it (presumably a pause as the news sinks in) makes it land harder. Highly quotable and very rewatchable.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Whoops.

jokes.text: 'It is if you're an elderly cokehead trying to launder money through a dummy soda corporation.'
jokes.setup: Frank says confusing Boca Raton with Boko Haram is 'an easy misunderstanding'
jokes.punchline: Dee lists all of Frank's specific crimes as the qualifying conditions for making such a misunderstanding
jokes.explanation: Solid construction — the punchline packs in cocaine use, age, money laundering, and corporate fraud in one economical sentence. Dee as the voice of incredulous reason is a good fit for this moment. Funny but not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: How do you confuse a city in Florida with a terrorist organization in Africa? It's an easy misunderstanding.

jokes.text: The reveal that Frank has multiple product lines beyond Wolf Cola — 'Frank's Fluids,' a 'Nip boba drink,' and Fight Milk
jokes.setup: Dennis notes this scandal will touch 'all of Frank's Fluids'
jokes.punchline: 'My God, there are other fluids?' — Dee's horror at learning the enterprise is bigger than anyone knew, compounded by the brand names themselves
jokes.explanation: Good escalation joke — 'Frank's Fluids' as an umbrella brand name is inherently funny and slightly disgusting. Dee's 'My God, there are other fluids?' is a great straight-woman reaction. Sets up the Fight Milk subplot neatly.

dialogue.line: It is if you're an elderly cokehead, trying to launder money through a dummy soda corporation.

jokes.text: Charlie and Mac's simultaneous shocked double-take upon hearing UFC fighters drink Fight Milk: 'Fight Milk?!' / 'Fight Milk?!'
jokes.setup: Frank casually mentions Fight Milk is selling to UFC fighters
jokes.punchline: Charlie and Mac's identical, synchronized outrage that their product is being sold without them — reaction beat implying they can't believe it
jokes.explanation: The synchronized reaction is funny precisely because it's so perfectly mirrored — Charlie and Mac as Fight Milk's indignant co-creators is very on-brand. Functional comedy, not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: My God, there are other fluids?

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie's circular logic about bodyguards and UFC fighters: 'The best bodyguards are former UFC fighters... and the best UFC fighters are former bodyguards... it's a revolving door.'
jokes.setup: Mac explains why UFC fighters would naturally drink Fight Milk, which was 'designed for bodyguards, by bodyguards'
jokes.punchline: Mac and Charlie build an entirely circular logical argument and both nod in complete agreement, convinced it makes sense
jokes.explanation: This is a beautifully structured idiot-logic joke. The argument is completely circular — 'bodyguards are UFC fighters, UFC fighters are bodyguards' — but Mac and Charlie deliver it with total conviction and Dennis doesn't even push back because he's already thinking about the brand. Perfect character integration: only Mac and Charlie could build this argument and find it persuasive.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Fight Milk?! Fight Milk?!

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, dude, that's our drink.

jokes.text: Frank tells Dee to dye his hair blond as part of his 'go bag' crisis response
jokes.setup: Frank pulls out a 'go bag' in response to the Wolf Cola crisis
jokes.punchline: His crisis preparedness involves going blond — suggesting Frank's go bag is for fleeing his identity, not the country
jokes.explanation: Good Frank-specific absurdism — the go bag implies prior planning, but the contents (hair dye) reveal his crisis response is comically superficial. Solid but not outstanding.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Remember, we designed that for bodyguards, by bodyguards. And it makes total sense because the-the best bodyguards are former UFC fighters. Well, of course. And the best UFC fighters are former bodyguards, so bodyguards, UFC fighters, that's like... It's a revolving door.

jokes.text: 'Oh, this is a good day for me' — Dee's gleeful reaction to learning Dennis is also implicated
jokes.setup: Dennis panics upon learning he's executive vice president of worldwide distribution
jokes.punchline: Dee's immediate, undisguised joy at Dennis's misfortune — before she gets pulled in too
jokes.explanation: Classic sibling dynamic comedy — Dee's delight is immediately punished when she's also named. The structure of the joke (gloat → reveal she's also trapped) is good, but the execution is fairly standard for the show.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Found my go bag. Dee, come over here and dye my hair blond.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Go bag? You're gonna go blond?

jokes.text: Frank explains he made Dennis VP because 'you wanted all the power so you could get the puss' and Dennis admits 'I only wanted the illusion of power. I never saw an ounce of puss.'
jokes.setup: Frank reveals Dennis is implicated because he's VP of worldwide distribution
jokes.punchline: The reason Dennis accepted the title was to attract women, and it completely failed — delivered with Dennis's wounded dignity intact
jokes.explanation: Very character-specific — Dennis's vanity and failed sexual strategizing is a core character trait. 'I never saw an ounce of puss' is a quotable, specific line that punctures Dennis's usual self-assurance. Good character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Remember when you wanted all the power so you could get the puss? I made you executive vice president of worldwide distribution.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Shit, but nobody knows that, right? I mean, dude, I only wanted the illusion of power. The-the illusion. I never saw an ounce of puss.

jokes.text: Dennis's big speech is interrupted by the reveal that they had to wait for him to finish at Bed Bath & Beyond
jokes.setup: Dennis dramatically announces they only have '24 hours' to respond, building to a tense declaration
jokes.punchline: Dee's flat 'This is why we had to wait for you to go to Bed Bath & Beyond?' undercuts the entire dramatic build
jokes.explanation: Perfect comic deflation. Dennis's cinematic self-importance is punctured by the mundanity of Bed Bath & Beyond. The specificity of that store is key — it's both extremely domestic and entirely at odds with Dennis's self-image. Good structure: the scene break [03:40] times the reveal perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: You're executive vice president of operations.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Oh. What? Yes. Goddamn it, Frank, why would you lump me into this?

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: It's a family business. I wanted it to be wholesome.

jokes.text: Frank makes Dee executive vice president of operations because 'it's a family business — I wanted it to be wholesome'
jokes.setup: Dee is gleefully watching Dennis's downfall when Frank reveals she's also named
jokes.punchline: Frank's justification — 'it's a family business, I wanted it to be wholesome' — is the most absurd possible reason for dragging her into a terrorist-soda scandal
jokes.explanation: 'I wanted it to be wholesome' applied to a money laundering front that became Boko Haram's official drink is a great ironic punchline. Frank's earnest delivery of 'wholesome' in this context is the core of the joke.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: 24 hours... This is why we had to wait for you to go to Bed Bath & Beyond?

jokes.text: Dennis's PR crisis playbook: 'Mercedes built Nazi tanks and the Jews are still driving their cars. Floyd Mayweather beat the shit out of multiple women and he's the highest paid athlete of all time. There's only one thing you can't come back from — banging kids.'
jokes.setup: Dennis confidently explains that you can recover from any PR crisis
jokes.punchline: His examples escalate from Nazi collaboration to domestic violence to child abuse — with the final verdict being a checklist of corporate survivability that is deeply disturbing delivered as business wisdom
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's strongest jokes. Dennis delivers a systematic analysis of PR survivability using genuinely dark real-world examples, treating them as business data. The escalating structure (Nazi collaboration → domestic violence → child abuse) is tight, and the fact that he's correct about all of it makes it uncomfortably funny. 'The only thing you can't come back from is banging kids' as a PR rubric is pitch-black and very Dennis. Earns its 8+.

dialogue.line: This is why we had to wait for you to go to Bed Bath & Beyond?

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Yes, bitch.

jokes.text: 'Well, what about the Catholic Church?' — Dee's immediate counter-example, and Dennis conceding 'they did sidestep banging kids pretty masterfully'
jokes.setup: Dennis declares child abuse is the one unforgivable PR sin
jokes.punchline: Dee immediately points to the Catholic Church as a counter-example; Dennis concedes they 'sidestepped it pretty masterfully' but notes they had 'billions of dollars at their disposal'
jokes.explanation: The Catholic Church callback is an excellent one-two punch. Dennis's immediate acknowledgment — 'they did sidestep banging kids pretty masterfully' — treats it with the same clinical PR analysis, which is funnier than outrage. The budget caveat ('billions of dollars') as the key variable in child abuse PR management is brilliantly horrible. Dee's straight-faced delivery of the counter-example makes it land even harder.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Christ, Mercedes built Nazi tanks, okay? And the Jews are still driving their cars around. Floyd Mayweather beat the shit out of multiple women and he's the highest paid athlete of all time. All right? There's only one thing you can't come back from... banging kids.

jokes.text: 'Time to stop eating your crow and start drinking your crow, everybody!' — Mac's Fight Milk pitch opener at the UFC gym
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie crash a UFC gym to promote Fight Milk
jokes.punchline: Mac's mangled version of 'eating crow' — recontextualizing the idiom to literally mean consuming crow products
jokes.explanation: Clever wordplay that works on two levels: it's an idiomatic misfire AND a literal product pitch. Mac delivers it with total confidence, which is key. The line is memorable and captures the character well.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Well, what about the Catholic Church?

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Hmm. That's a good point. Yeah, no, they did sidestep banging kids pretty masterfully, but they've got billions of dollars at their disposal and we do not, so...

jokes.text: Mac's Fight Milk pitch: 'I've always been very passionate about dominating other men. There's nothing like the feeling of another man submitting to your will. In a lot of ways, that's love.'
jokes.setup: Mac begins pitching Fight Milk to UFC fighters
jokes.punchline: Mac's homoerotic framing of fighting — delivered completely sincerely, with zero self-awareness — before Charlie whispers 'he's a bodyguard though'
jokes.explanation: Very high character integration — Mac's deeply repressed homosexuality being accidentally expressed through his fighting rhetoric is a long-running character truth. 'In a lot of ways, that's love' is the peak. Charlie's panicked clarification ('he's a bodyguard though') makes it funnier. This joke could ONLY be Mac.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Time to stop eating your crow and start drinking your crow, everybody.

jokes.text: Charlie's Fight Milk pitch: 'We're a couple of crow enthusiasts who wanted to take the power and essence of a crow and pack that into a delicious milk drink that we invented, thus Fight Milk.'
jokes.setup: Charlie jumps in to rescue Mac's disastrous pitch
jokes.punchline: Charlie's explanation is somehow more confusing and less convincing than Mac's homoerotic tangent
jokes.explanation: 'Crow enthusiasts' and 'thus Fight Milk' are great Charlie-specific verbal tics. The fact that this is meant to be the RESCUE of the pitch and is still baffling is the core comedy. Very Charlie.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Now, I've always been very passionate about dominating other men.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Uh-oh.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: There's nothing like the feeling of another man submitting to your will. Now that's power. Yeah. In a lot of ways, that's love.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: What are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Okay, he's a bodyguard, though.

jokes.text: Cowboy Cerrone and Paul Felder are found in bathroom stalls violently sick, and Cerrone says 'I'd get up and shake your hands if I wasn't shitting my brains out right now'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are excited to meet the UFC fighters who love Fight Milk
jokes.punchline: The fighters are using it as a violent laxative to cut weight before the weigh-in — not because it's good
jokes.explanation: Great misdirection: Mac and Charlie's excitement at their brand success is immediately deflated by the discovery that the product is being used as a diarrhea aid. 'I'd get up and shake your hands if I wasn't shitting my brains out' is a great line and uses a real UFC fighter as the delivery mechanism, which adds an extra layer of comedic credibility.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: We're-we're a couple of crow enthusiasts who wanted to take the power and essence of a crow and-and we packed that into a delicious milk drink that we invented, thus Fight Milk.

jokes.text: Cerrone explains Fight Milk's weight-cutting utility: 'Makes you expel all body fluids. Sweat, piss, and shit — we got these weigh-ins coming up. Nothing cuts weight like Fight Milk.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are horrified their product makes people sick
jokes.punchline: Cerrone reframes the product's catastrophic side effects as a feature, delivered with the matter-of-fact calm of a professional athlete discussing his training regimen
jokes.explanation: The reframing of explosive illness as a sports nutrition benefit is a great comedic inversion. 'Nothing cuts weight like Fight Milk' as an earnest endorsement from a bathroom stall is the perfect deadpan delivery.

dialogue.speaker: Cowboy Cerrone
dialogue.line: Yeah, man, I'd get up and shake your hands if I wasn't shitting my brains out right now.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Oh, no.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: No, no, that's fine, yeah.

jokes.text: 'Oh, I just puked on my dick! Rock and roll.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are absorbing the news that Fight Milk is a violent weight-cut tool while standing in the bathroom
jokes.punchline: Felder's off-screen mid-conversation vomit, with his immediate philosophical acceptance of it
jokes.explanation: Possibly the single funniest line reading in the episode. The specificity of 'on my dick' (not just 'on myself'), combined with the immediate 'Rock and roll' acceptance, is comedy gold. It's grotesque, unexpected, perfectly economical, and highly quotable. Mac and Charlie's 'Rock and roll. All right, cool.' responses in kind make it even better. This earns its 8+ comfortably.

dialogue.line: Makes you expel all body fluids. Sweat, piss, and shit; we got these weigh-ins coming up. Nothing cuts weight like Fight Milk.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie awkwardly present Fight Milk merch (a water bottle) to two athletes actively vomiting
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are losing the room as the fighters vomit around them
jokes.punchline: Their commitment to the brand pitch despite the chaos — presenting a water bottle as merch while someone retches
jokes.explanation: Good cringe comedy — the gap between their professionalism (presenting merch) and the horror of the situation is funny. 'Um... yeah, water bottle' as a product pitch is pathetic in the best way.

dialogue.speaker: Fighter
dialogue.line: Oh, I just puked on my dick! Rock and roll.

jokes.text: Frank's PR strategy: 'I think how we do that is soften their brand.' 'Whose brand?' 'Boko Haram.'
jokes.setup: The gang prepares for their TV appearance to do damage control
jokes.punchline: Frank's solution to the Wolf Cola crisis is to rehabilitate the image of the terrorist organization — not distance from them
jokes.explanation: The reveal lands perfectly because Frank's business logic is internally consistent — the problem is Boko Haram's reputation, so fix Boko Haram's reputation. The beat-pause before 'Boko Haram' is essential. This is very Frank: he's not stupid, he's operating on a completely different moral axis. One of the episode's stronger conceptual jokes.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: You want to change... the perception of a global terrorist organization?

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Yeah, and I've got many facts to do it.

jokes.text: Dennis's PR strategy for Dee: 'You have a very important job... to say nothing and stand behind me. Audiences are gonna trust me over you because you're a woman, and by definition, shrill.'
jokes.setup: Dennis is orchestrating the TV appearance and assigns Dee a role
jokes.punchline: Dee's role is literally to stand silently and look supportive because Dennis believes audiences inherently distrust women — delivered with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: Classic Dennis narcissism — he has an entire theory of media reception that places him at the center of trustworthiness. 'By definition, shrill' as a matter-of-fact categorization is good. Dee's counter-argument ('women identify with women in power') followed by Dennis and Mac both immediately disagreeing is a nice extra beat.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: You see, audiences are gonna trust me over you because you're a woman, and, by definition, shrill.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: No. Women identify with women in power.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Oh, no, Dee. Women hate other women in power. I'm threatened by 'em. Everyone is.

jokes.text: Mac and Dennis both instantly agreeing that 'women hate other women in power' and 'I'm threatened by them, everyone is'
jokes.setup: Dee argues that women in power resonate with female audiences
jokes.punchline: Mac enthusiastically agrees that women hate other women in power, and Dennis co-signs 'everyone is' — both completely missing any self-reflection
jokes.explanation: Good but not exceptional — Mac and Dennis's casual misogyny is well-established show territory. The specificity of Mac saying 'I'm threatened by them' (as a man who is threatened by women in power) adds a touch of absurdist self-revelation.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Now, objectify yourself and humanize me.

jokes.text: On live TV, Dennis delivers a smooth non-apology, Dee robotically says 'I'm just here to humanize him' and 'to support him' when prompted
jokes.setup: Dennis's plan is for Dee to stand silently behind him in support
jokes.punchline: Dee follows the instructions so robotically that when she speaks it sounds like a hostage statement, and she parrots 'to support him' after Dennis corrects her 'to humanize him'
jokes.explanation: Good execution of Dennis's control-freak strategy playing out in real time. The fact that Dee gets the line wrong ('humanize' vs 'support') and has to be corrected on live television is a nice humiliating beat.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Women identify with women in power.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Oh, no, Dee. Women hate other women in power. I'm threatened by 'em. Everyone is.

jokes.text: Dennis, on live TV, announces that a portion of Wolf Cola proceeds will go to 'a charity supporting African people — all Africans, even our friends at Boko Haram, because they are people, too. We don't discriminate.'
jokes.setup: Dennis is in the middle of a smooth corporate damage-control interview
jokes.punchline: His charity announcement explicitly includes Boko Haram as beneficiaries — framing terrorism as a diversity inclusion issue
jokes.explanation: The pivot from corporate charity-washing to explicitly including a terrorist organization as beneficiaries under a 'we don't discriminate' banner is sharp, dark, and funny. Dennis's oblivious sincerity in including Boko Haram in his diversity statement is the joke working on a satirical level about how performative corporate charity language can be stretched to absurdity. Earns its 8+.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: And also, we're sorry. We accept full responsibility for this heinous mistake, and please know that I am actively firing people as we speak, because I am the boss. Bitch.

jokes.text: Frank, on live TV, launches into a Boko Haram defense: 'Boko Haram did not do 9/11. That was al-Qaeda. Paris was ISIS. Boko Haram is just concentrating on Africa. There are mosquitos down there that are bigger terrorists than Boko Haram.'
jokes.setup: The TV interview is going smoothly; Dennis tries to end it
jokes.punchline: Frank hijacks the interview to defend Boko Haram's reputation with factual accuracy — culminating in mosquitos being 'bigger terrorists than Boko Haram'
jokes.explanation: This is the payoff to Frank's earlier 'soften their brand' strategy, and it delivers brilliantly. The joke works because Frank is TECHNICALLY CORRECT about everything — Boko Haram didn't do 9/11 or the Paris attacks — but deploying this geopolitical precision in a TV damage control segment makes it catastrophically worse. 'Mosquitos are bigger terrorists than Boko Haram' is an inspired kicker. Very quotable, very rewatchable. One of the episode's best moments.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: You know what, Chet, can I say something? I think we've said enough. I think... you got to understand that Boko Haram did not do 9/11. Yeah. That was... al-Qaeda. Paris, that was done by ISIS. Boko Haram is just concentrating, they're doing Africa. I mean... I mean, there's mosquitos down there that are bigger terrorists than Boko Haram.

jokes.text: 'We're gonna take a break.' — the host's immediate cut to commercial after Frank's Boko Haram defense
jokes.setup: Frank has just defended Boko Haram on live television
jokes.punchline: The host's instant, emotionless 'We're gonna take a break' — the universal TV signal for 'everything has gone wrong'
jokes.explanation: Perfectly timed punctuation joke. The host's flat delivery is the right beat after Frank's escalating defense. The scene cut itself is the punchline — we don't need anything more.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Boko Haram did not do 9/11. That was... al-Qaeda. Paris, that was done by ISIS. Boko Haram is just concentrating, they're doing Africa.

jokes.text: 'And the 24-hour news cycle starts again.' — Dennis's immediate pivot back to crisis mode after their catastrophic TV appearance
jokes.setup: Dennis earlier explained they had 24 hours to control the narrative
jokes.punchline: After comprehensively making everything worse on TV, Dennis resets the clock with his PR framework still intact, as if the framework is the problem
jokes.explanation: Good callback — the 24-hour clock resets after they've catastrophically failed, and Dennis's response is to restart the cycle rather than question his approach. Character-consistent comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: People calling me a bitch, flat-chested bitch, pretty much everybody wanting to rape me.

jokes.text: Dee reports being called 'bitch, flat-chested bitch' and that 'pretty much everybody' wants to rape her online after the TV appearance
jokes.setup: The gang assesses the fallout from their TV appearance
jokes.punchline: Dee's matter-of-fact catalog of the specific forms of online harassment she's receiving — delivered as a data report, not an emotional plea
jokes.explanation: Topical and dark — the show's critique of online harassment is handled through Dee's characteristic detachment. Dennis's immediate pivot to explain why this is her fault (she apologized) makes it funnier and more character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Now social media will come down on you with the fury of a middle-aged man who's accomplished nothing.

jokes.text: Dee reports being called 'bitch, flat-chested bitch' and 'pretty much everybody wanting to rape me' on social media — Dennis says 'You opened that door the second you apologized'
jokes.setup: Dee apologized on TV against Dennis's advice
jokes.punchline: Dennis frames the horrific online abuse Dee is receiving as a predictable, logical consequence of her PR error — not as something inherently wrong
jokes.explanation: Darkly funny because Dennis is simultaneously wrong (there's no PR justification for rape threats) and weirdly correct (apologizing did escalate the pile-on). His detachment from the horror of Dee's experience is the joke. Satirizes both online mob behavior and Dennis's sociopathy.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Are you fat? You probably are, 'cause you're watching TV! Or Internet.

jokes.text: Dennis explains online harassment: 'People need an outlet to unleash their rage. Social media will come down on you with the fury of a middle-aged man who's accomplished nothing.'
jokes.setup: Dee is upset about being harassed online
jokes.punchline: Dennis's sociological theory of internet rage as the displaced fury of mediocre men — delivered with complete confidence and insight that Dennis himself seems unaware applies to him
jokes.explanation: One of the more prescient and quotable lines in the episode. 'The fury of a middle-aged man who's accomplished nothing' is sharp social commentary that also quietly describes Dennis and Frank. The line has aged well and captures something true about online culture.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: It's easy for us men... we have four acceptable body types. Skinny ripped, jack ripped, dad bod, and fat... if you're funny. It's a landslide! As we all know, women only have one acceptable body type. Skinny, big tits!

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie burst in with crow traps, declaring 'Fight Milk is boomin' — apparently people are using it to lose weight
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie left the bathroom scene with their Fight Milk dreams apparently crushed
jokes.punchline: They've pivoted immediately to expanding the brand based on the diarrhea use case — carrying literal crow traps
jokes.explanation: Good energy pivot — they've internalized the diarrhea-as-feature business model and are now scaling up. The crow traps as a prop are a nice visual detail. Consistent with their entrepreneurial obliviousness.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Aah! No nerds! Fight Milk!

jokes.text: Frank: 'The fastest-growing marketplace is Muslim extremists.' Dennis: 'Frank, we're not going into business with terrorists!'
jokes.setup: The gang discusses next steps for Wolf Cola
jokes.punchline: Frank identifies Boko Haram as a growth market to double down on rather than flee from
jokes.explanation: Frank's growth-market framing of radical Islamic extremism is very on-brand for his character — amoral capitalism applied without any filter. 'The fastest-growing marketplace' as a clinical description of terrorist recruitment is darkly funny.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Really, I mean, between the three of you, we could be opening up a bakery with all the muffin tops I'm seeing.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie's Fight Milk infomercial: 'Are you fat? You probably are, 'cause you're watching TV!'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie announce they're taking over the bar's TV set for their Fight Milk rebrand campaign
jokes.punchline: Their infomercial opens by insulting the viewer directly — the worst possible marketing approach
jokes.explanation: Opening a product pitch by telling your target audience they're fat is a great comedic inversion of advertising logic. 'Or Internet' as a tag is a nice extra beat. Very Mac and Charlie — their total lack of marketing instincts is the character-based comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: No! We're not the diarrhea guys.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: No!

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: That's not what I want to be.

jokes.text: Mac's infomercial segment: 'It's easy for us men — we have four acceptable body types: skinny ripped, jack ripped, dad bod, and fat... if you're funny.'
jokes.setup: Mac begins a segment on women's bodies for the Fight Milk rebrand
jokes.punchline: His taxonomy of male body types is delivered as self-evident truth, with 'fat — if you're funny' as the charitable exception
jokes.explanation: Good observational-comedy construction — 'fat, if you're funny' as the loophole in male body standards is a sharp and true observation. The setup also works as a contrast to the women's section that follows.

dialogue.speaker: Ring Girl
dialogue.line: We're not into your weird diarrhea drink.

jokes.text: Mac's infomercial: 'As we all know, women only have one acceptable body type: skinny, big tits!' Cut to Charlie claiming crow enzymes will 'enlargify' their breasts.
jokes.setup: Mac's infomercial contrasts flexible male body standards with the single female standard
jokes.punchline: Charlie's pseudo-scientific 'enlargify' claim for crow eggs, combined with 'No nerds! Fight Milk!'
jokes.explanation: 'Enlargify' is a great Charlie word — confident malapropism that perfectly encapsulates his pseudo-scientific approach to Fight Milk. 'No nerds! Fight Milk!' as an edit cut is chaotic and very on-brand for the infomercial format they're attempting.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: It's not for women! It was never made for women! But it'd be great if women also drank it. The dream was to create a muscle-up energy drink that gave you the power to fight like a crow!

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Yes! Men! Or women. But yes. But definitely crow-power fighting skills.

jokes.text: 'New evidence is suggesting that all this science inside one crow's egg can scientifically make your breasts larger. Watch the enzymes enlargify your breasts.'
jokes.setup: Mac has just described the ideal female body type
jokes.punchline: Charlie's infomercial claim that crow eggs can 'enlargify' breasts — using a made-up word with casual scientific authority
jokes.explanation: 'Enlargify' is a great Charlie word — combining 'enlarge' and 'amplify' into a word that sounds almost plausible. The phrase 'all this science inside one crow's egg' delivered as if it's self-evident is very Charlie. His semi-literacy combined with false confidence is the joke.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Well, if you're asking me if I like wild animals slobbering all over me, then, yeah, I guess I'm not really a... not really a dog lover then.

jokes.text: Mac's fight pitch to UFC ring girls, pointing a laser pointer at their bodies: 'Honestly ladies, you could afford to lose a few pounds — maybe in this area, or here. Between the three of you, we could be opening a bakery with all the muffin tops I'm seeing.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are pitching Fight Milk to UFC ring girls as their new female market
jokes.punchline: Mac produces a laser pointer to indicate specific areas of the women's bodies he finds unacceptable, while comparing them to baked goods
jokes.explanation: Classic cringe-discomfort escalation. The laser pointer specifically is the detail that elevates this from standard uncomfortable to genuinely absurd — who brings a laser pointer to a marketing pitch? Charlie's apology ('I didn't realize he brought a laser pointer') implies even he didn't know, adding an extra layer.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I should be able to eat me some fried dog. Know what I'm saying? I should be able to eat a bucket of fried dog at a chicken fight.

jokes.text: 'Between the three of you, we could be opening a bakery with all the muffin tops I'm seeing.'
jokes.setup: Mac is 'helpfully' explaining why the ring girls should drink Fight Milk
jokes.punchline: The 'bakery' metaphor — taking 'muffin top' (the body-shaming term) and extending it into an actual business proposition
jokes.explanation: The 'opening a bakery' extension of the muffin top metaphor shows actual joke craft — not just using the insult but pushing it into a new domain. Mac's earnestness makes it worse in the best way.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: 'cause that's just the crow eggs and some of the crow's fecal matter.

jokes.text: Ring girl rejects Fight Milk: 'We're not into your weird diarrhea drink.' Charlie: 'It's not a diarrhea drink!' Mac: 'That's not what I want to be!'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie have just humiliated themselves pitching to ring girls
jokes.punchline: Their product has already been tagged publicly as a diarrhea drink — and Mac's wounded identity crisis ('That's not what I want to be!') is funnier than any factual denial
jokes.explanation: Mac's existential crisis about being 'the diarrhea guys' is a great character beat. The escalating denials land well, and 'That's not what I want to be' has a genuine pathos that makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: UFC Official
dialogue.line: What the hell is going on? Who are these guys?

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Uh, just like to take the opportunity to thank Fight Milk.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Yes, and thank you, Cowboy, and thank you, Megan.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: We'd also like to take this opportunity to announce that Fight Milk is now the official drink of the UFC.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Official drink.

dialogue.speaker: UFC Official
dialogue.line: No, no. This is not the official drink of the UFC. And I don't know who these guys are. Security, get these assholes out of here!

jokes.text: "It's not a diarrhea drink!" / "We're not the diarrhea guys!" — Mac and Charlie's horrified rejection of this identity
jokes.setup: The ring girl calls Fight Milk 'your weird diarrhea drink'
jokes.punchline: Mac and Charlie are more horrified at being called 'the diarrhea guys' than at any actual problem with the product
jokes.explanation: Their wounded pride about the 'diarrhea guys' label — given that Fight Milk literally functions as an emetic/laxative — is a great irony. The callback to Fight Milk's established weight-cutting function makes this land harder. Character integration is excellent: they care about identity over reality.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Turns out there are two things that can't be forgiven... raping children and disliking dogs.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie's Fight Milk origin speech: 'The dream was to create a muscle-up energy drink that gave you the power to fight like a crow!'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie argue they're not 'the diarrhea guys'
jokes.punchline: Their actual stated vision — the power to 'fight like a crow' — is somehow more absurd and less marketable than the diarrhea angle
jokes.explanation: The clarification of what Fight Milk was SUPPOSED to be is somehow worse than what it became. 'The power to fight like a crow' is pure Charlie/Mac absurdist logic. The fact that they're defending this as the superior brand identity over 'diarrhea drink' is the core comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: We pumped it full of human growth hormone, you know.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I mean, just nothing else was working. It just... it was just giving people diarrhea.

jokes.text: 'We got to get back to the lab. We got to get some more crows.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie have failed completely with the ring girls pitch
jokes.punchline: Charlie's response to total failure is to restart product development — specifically, acquiring more crows
jokes.explanation: 'We got to get some more crows' as a business solution is perfect Charlie logic. The specificity — it's not 'more ingredients' but specifically more crows — is very character-specific. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: If you give it enough time, something new will come along to replace peoples' old outrage with new outrage.

jokes.text: Second TV appearance: Dee again parrots 'I'm just here to humanize him. To support him. To-to support him.' while being corrected mid-sentence by Dennis
jokes.setup: Second TV appearance — same setup as before
jokes.punchline: Dee repeats the same hostage-statement line but gets corrected again in real time by Dennis, making the humiliation worse
jokes.explanation: Functional running gag — the second iteration loses some freshness but the mid-sentence correction adds a new layer of indignity. The diminishing returns are intentional.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Goddamn it!

jokes.text: A dog escapes onto the TV set. Dennis reveals he doesn't like dogs. Host reacts: 'I have never met a person who does not like dogs before.'
jokes.setup: A dog wanders onto the set during the interview; Dennis asks it to be removed
jokes.punchline: The host's horror at Dennis not liking dogs dwarfs his earlier concern about Wolf Cola's terrorist ties
jokes.explanation: Great comedic social commentary built into character comedy. The host's equanimity during the terrorist soda scandal but complete shock at someone not liking dogs is a sharp observation about media priorities. Dennis's subsequent defensive monologue about not being judged ('we're just afraid to admit it') adds more layers.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Start the clock.

dialogue.speaker: Unknown
dialogue.line: Yeah.

jokes.text: Dennis's escalating argument: 'If you can eat fried chicken, then I should be able to eat me some fried dog. I should be able to eat a bucket of fried dog at a chicken fight.'
jokes.setup: Dennis defends not liking dogs by calling out the hypocrisy of people who oppose dogfighting but eat chicken
jokes.punchline: His logical argument inverts the food/fighting relationship — fried dog at a chicken fight — which is technically the same equivalence he's arguing for but sounds maximally offensive
jokes.explanation: Dennis's argument is internally logical but each step makes it worse. 'A bucket of fried dog at a chicken fight' is an outstanding line — it's the precise inverse of fried chicken at a dogfight, delivered as the natural endpoint of his reasoning. High originality, strong structure, very quotable. Dennis at his most dangerous-smart. Earns its 8+.

jokes.text: 'So are you saying you're an animal rights activist?' / 'No, I'm actually the opposite, pal. I can't imagine a bigger waste of people's time and energy.'
jokes.setup: Frank has been making what sounds like animal welfare arguments
jokes.punchline: Frank clarifies he's the exact opposite of an animal rights activist — his argument was for consistent cruelty, not consistent compassion
jokes.explanation: Good subversion — Frank's argument genuinely sounded like it was building toward animal rights advocacy, so the reversal ('I'm the opposite') lands well. His follow-up dismissal of animal rights as a 'waste of time' is characteristically Frank.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie reveal their two-step Fight Milk weight-cutting process: 'crow loading' (four to five whole ground-up crows) followed by Fight Milk Classic (crow eggs and 'some of the crow's fecal matter')
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are explaining why the UFC fighters aren't purging yet
jokes.punchline: The 'two-step process' escalates from 'crow loading' (disgusting) to Fight Milk Classic containing crow feces (catastrophically disgusting), delivered as scientific nutrition advice
jokes.explanation: The clinical nutrition explanation of a beverage containing crow feces is a great escalation joke. 'Some of the crow's fecal matter' delivered with the same earnestness as a supplement label is the peak. 'You'll be puking on your dick in no time' as an encouraging sign-off is a callback to Felder's earlier line and lands perfectly. High character integration — only Charlie constructs nutrition science this way.

jokes.text: 'You're gonna be puking on your dick in no time.' — Charlie's encouraging send-off to the UFC fighters
jokes.setup: Charlie is reassuring the fighters that the product will work
jokes.punchline: He uses 'puking on your dick' as a benchmark of success and delivers it as an affectionate motivational phrase
jokes.explanation: Perfect callback to Felder's earlier line, now repurposed as an encouraging phrase — 'you're gonna be puking on your dick in no time' has the warmth and cadence of a coach saying 'you're gonna crush it.' Very quotable, very rewatchable. The callback elevates it beyond the original.

jokes.text: 'We got to get him on Fight Milk, man.' — Mac and Charlie immediately eyeing Cub Swanson at the weigh-in
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are at the UFC weigh-in rooting for Cowboy
jokes.punchline: Even in this high-stakes moment, their primary focus is expanding their client base
jokes.explanation: Minor joke — it's a quick character beat showing their priorities are still on expansion even at a critical moment. Functional but not especially memorable.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie's pre-celebration: 'This is gonna change Fight Milk and our lives forever' / 'I've already scoped out every single exit' (in case they have to bolt)
jokes.setup: Waiting for Cowboy to make weight
jokes.punchline: Charlie has simultaneously prepared for triumph and escape — he's already mapped the exits in case they need to run, while Mac talks about changing their lives
jokes.explanation: Good character beat — Charlie's pragmatic cowardice ('I've already scoped every exit') contrasted with Mac's big dreams is a solid character dynamic. Slightly underbaked but lands.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie crash the UFC weigh-in press conference to announce Fight Milk as 'the official drink of the UFC' while the UFC commissioner tells them he has no idea who they are and calls security
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie have been celebrating Cowboy making weight
jokes.punchline: Their unauthorized announcement is immediately contradicted and they are removed by security while chanting 'Fight Milk!' — the ultimate brand humiliation
jokes.explanation: Great escalating cringe sequence — the gap between Mac and Charlie's triumphant announcement and the immediate humiliating reality is perfectly constructed. The 'Fight Milk! Fight Milk!' chant as they're dragged out is the right note to end the sequence on.

jokes.text: 'Turns out there are two things that can't be forgiven — raping children and disliking dogs.'
jokes.setup: Frank's dislike of dogs on TV has apparently destroyed Wolf Cola's reputation completely
jokes.punchline: Dennis's callback to his own 'one thing you can't come back from' thesis — now revised to include not liking dogs, placed on equal footing with child abuse
jokes.explanation: One of the strongest jokes in the episode and an excellent structural callback. The original joke established one absolute moral floor (child abuse); now Dennis is forced to revise it to add 'disliking dogs' at the same level. The absurdity of that equivalence — placing animal preference alongside child abuse as equally unforgivable — is sharp social commentary about the internet's value hierarchy. Well-structured, quotable, and pays off earlier setup. Earns the 8+ rating.

jokes.text: 'Turns out there are two things that can't be forgiven — raping children and disliking dogs.'
jokes.setup: Dennis earlier said the only unforgivable PR sin was child abuse; he's now also being destroyed online for not liking dogs
jokes.punchline: He updates his PR rubric to include dog-hating alongside child abuse — the equivalence is both darkly funny and a pointed media critique
jokes.explanation: This is the best joke in the episode. The callback structure is perfect: Dennis established his PR rubric in act one (child abuse = only unforgivable sin), and now he updates it to add dog-hating at equivalent moral weight. The structure generates the comedy — not through shock but through the precision of the update and what it says about media priorities. Highly quotable, strong rewatch value. The economy is exceptional: one sentence does enormous comedic and satirical work.

jokes.text: News report reveals Fight Milk caused UFC fighters to test positive for banned substances — it was 'pumped full of human growth hormone' because 'nothing else was working, it was just giving people diarrhea'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are celebrating their weigh-in victory
jokes.punchline: Their product has caused a doping scandal because they secretly added HGH as a workaround for the diarrhea problem
jokes.explanation: 'Nothing else was working, it was just giving people diarrhea' as the casual explanation for why they added HGH is great character comedy. Their problem-solving logic (just add human growth hormone) is exactly right for Charlie and Mac.

jokes.text: Dee's reaction to the Fight Milk scandal: 'You guys, this is good! This is good. We're freed and they are screwed.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie's Fight Milk scandal breaks just as they're celebrating
jokes.punchline: Dee immediately recognizes this as her escape hatch — Fight Milk news replaces Wolf Cola news in the cycle
jokes.explanation: Good character beat for Dee — her willingness to celebrate Charlie and Mac's downfall as her salvation is on-brand. Functional but not exceptional.

jokes.text: Dennis explains the 24-hour news cycle resolution: 'If you give it enough time, something new will come along to replace people's old outrage with new outrage.' — immediately followed by the news report naming Frank's Fluids as Fight Milk's parent company
jokes.setup: Dennis explains that the news cycle will eventually save them
jokes.punchline: The new outrage immediately circles back to Frank's Fluids — his moment of wisdom is punctured in real time
jokes.explanation: Perfect structural irony — Dennis's one moment of genuine media insight is immediately destroyed by the news cycle doing exactly what he predicted, but pointing back at them. The callback to Frank's Fluids as the parent company is a great closing loop. The timing of the news report cutting him off mid-relief is well-constructed.

jokes.text: News report reveals Fight Milk is 'made right here in Philadelphia by a parent company known as Frank's Fluids' — connecting both storylines
jokes.setup: Dennis has just celebrated that Wolf Cola's crisis is over because Fight Milk's scandal replaced it
jokes.punchline: The news immediately reveals Frank's Fluids (Wolf Cola's parent) made Fight Milk — both scandals are now one scandal
jokes.explanation: Good structural payoff — the episode's two plotlines (Wolf Cola/Boko Haram and Fight Milk/HGH) are merged through the Frank's Fluids connection. The timing is perfect: Dennis's premature relief is immediately destroyed. 'Goddamn it, Frank!' as the final beat is well-earned.

jokes.text: 'Start the clock.' — Dennis's immediate pivot back to 24-hour crisis mode as the new scandal breaks
jokes.setup: Dennis just finished explaining how the news cycle would save them
jokes.punchline: 'Start the clock' — Dennis immediately reactivates his failed PR framework the second it's needed again, with no self-reflection
jokes.explanation: Two words, maximum economy. 'Start the clock' reactivates every element of Dennis's earlier failed 24-hour plan simultaneously, with zero acknowledgment that the plan didn't work. Perfect character encapsulation. The confidence in the face of total failure is what makes Dennis funny, and this two-word button nails it.

jokes.text: 'Goddamn it!' — Frank's single-word reaction as he realizes Fight Milk's PR nightmare has just been linked back to Wolf Cola via Frank's Fluids
jokes.setup: Everyone momentarily thinks they're off the hook; news report names Frank's Fluids as Fight Milk's parent company
jokes.punchline: Frank's instant deflation — 'Goddamn it!' — mirrors his earlier 'Whoops' and closes the episode on the same note it opened on
jokes.explanation: Good closing punctuation joke. The parallel to 'Whoops' at the episode's start gives it structural resonance — Frank begins and ends with inadequate single-word responses to catastrophic business news. 'Start the clock' from Dennis right before it sets it up perfectly.

tmdb_overview: Franks Fluids LLC is in big trouble after a news segment. Dee and Dennis help with the PR nightmare and Charlie and Mac work on a scheme to make Fight Milk the official drink of the UFC.
